method_card.title: How to Use BIDMAS (Order of Operations)
steps: Then Division and Multiplication, left to right.
Then Addition and Subtraction, left to right.
method_card.content:
BIDMAS (also called BODMAS) gives the order to work in: Brackets, Indices, Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction.

Division and multiplication share one level: do them left to right, not multiplication first. Addition and subtraction share the next level, also left to right.

A fraction bar groups its top and bottom like brackets: evaluate each fully, then divide. A root counts as an index.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Multiply and divide before you add and subtract; work left to right within each pair.
problem_bank.silver_description: Brackets and powers first, then multiply and divide, then add and subtract, left to right.
problem_bank.gold_description: Multi step calculations with fraction bars, roots, nested powers and brackets.

bronze.hint: Do the multiplication before the addition.

misconceptions.message: Multiplication comes first: 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 + 10 = 13. Adding 3 + 5 first gives 16, which ignores the order.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: No brackets or powers. Multiplication comes before addition, so clear the × first.

guided_steps.hint: It should match your last line.
guided_steps.done: The × was done before the +, so 13 is right.

bronze.hint: Do the multiplication before the subtraction.

misconceptions.message: Multiply first: 4 × 3 = 12, then 20 − 12 = 8. Doing 20 − 4 first, then × 3, gives 48.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Multiplication comes before subtraction, so do the × first.

guided_steps.done: The × was cleared before the −.

bronze.hint: Do the division before the addition.

misconceptions.message: Divide first: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, then 6 + 3 = 9. Adding 6 + 12 first, then ÷ 4, gives 4.5.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Division comes before addition, so do the ÷ first.

guided_steps.done: The ÷ was done before the +.

bronze.hint: Multiply first, then subtract in the order written.

misconceptions.message: Subtract in the order written: 8 × 3 = 24, then 24 − 10 = 14. Doing 10 − 24 gives −14.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Multiplication comes before subtraction. Clear the × first, then subtract in the order written.

bronze.hint: Do the division and the multiplication, then add.

misconceptions.message: Do 15 ÷ 3 = 5 and 4 × 3 = 12 first, then 5 + 12 = 17. Working straight left to right gives 27.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Two high priority operations, one ÷ and one ×. Clear BOTH before adding.

guided_steps.done: Both × and ÷ were done before the +.

bronze.hint: Work out both multiplications, then add.

misconceptions.message: Both multiplications come before the addition: 2 × 7 = 14 and 3 × 4 = 12, then 14 + 12 = 26. Working straight left to right gives 68.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Two multiplications and one addition. Clear BOTH multiplications before adding.

guided_steps.done: Both × were done before the +.

bronze.hint: Multiply first, then subtract and add left to right.

misconceptions.message: Clear the × first: 5 × 4 = 20, then 30 − 20 + 1 = 11. Working straight left to right gives 101.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: One multiplication in the middle. Clear it, then work − and + left to right.

guided_steps.done: Left to right stops you subtracting 21 by mistake.

bronze.hint: Two divisions have equal priority, so go left to right.

misconceptions.message: Two divisions are equal priority, so go left to right: 48 ÷ 6 = 8, then 8 ÷ 2 = 4. Doing 6 ÷ 2 first gives 48 ÷ 3 = 16.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Two divisions. They are equal priority, so work strictly left to right.

guided_steps.done: Left to right, not 6 ÷ 2 first.

misconceptions.message: Brackets first: 3 + 5 = 8, then 8 × 4 = 32. Skipping the bracket to do 5 × 4 first gives 23.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Brackets first, always.

guided_steps.done: The bracket was done before the ×.

silver.hint: Brackets first, then multiply, then add.

misconceptions.message: Brackets first: 12 − 4 = 8, then 5 × 8 = 40, then 40 + 6 = 46. Ignoring the bracket to read 5 × 12 − 4 + 6 gives 62.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket first, then multiply, then add.

guided_steps.done: Bracket, then ×, then +.

silver.hint: Do the power and the multiplication before the addition.

misconceptions.message: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3 = 6. With 8 the answer is 8 + 15 = 23. Using 6 gives 21.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Do the power and the multiplication before the addition.

guided_steps.done: Power and × first, then +.

silver.hint: Brackets first, then divide and multiply left to right.

misconceptions.message: Brackets first: 4 + 6 = 10, then 100 ÷ 10 = 10 and 10 × 3 = 30. Splitting it as 100 ÷ 4 + 6 × 3 gives 43.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket first, then ÷ and × left to right.

guided_steps.done: Divide before multiply because it is on the left.

silver.hint: Do the power first, then multiply, then subtract.

misconceptions.message: The index applies only to the 4, not to 3 × 4. So 4² = 16, then 3 × 16 = 48, then 48 − 20 = 28. Squaring 3 × 4 as 12² gives 124.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: The power sits on the 4 only. Do it first, then multiply, then subtract.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply 3 by 16. The power was only on the 4.

guided_steps.done: The index was on the 4 alone, then × then −.

silver.hint: Work inside the brackets, then square the whole bracket, then add.

misconceptions.message: (7 − 3)² means 4² = 16, not 7² − 3² = 40. So the answer is 16 + 8 = 24. Squaring each number gives 40 + 8 = 48.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Bracket first, then square the whole bracket, then add.

guided_steps.hint: Square the whole bracket, not each number.

guided_steps.done: The bracket was squared as a whole, then +.

silver.hint: Finish the bracket (power then add), then multiply, then subtract.

misconceptions.message: 3² means 3 × 3 = 9, not 3 × 2 = 6. With 9 the bracket is 10, so 60 − 2 × 10 = 40. Using 6 gives a bracket of 7 and 60 − 14 = 46.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Work inside the bracket first (its power, then its add), then multiply, then subtract.

guided_steps.done: Bracket (power then add) first, then × then −.

gold.hint: The fraction bar groups the top and the bottom: finish each, then divide.

misconceptions.message: The bar groups the top and bottom: (36 − 12) ÷ (2 × 3) = 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Reading it inline as 6² − 12 ÷ 2 × 3 gives 36 − 18 = 18.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: The fraction bar groups the top and the bottom. Finish each, then divide.

guided_steps.done: Top and bottom were grouped before dividing.

gold.hint: Build the fraction fully (bracket, power, divide), then add the 5.

misconceptions.message: You found the fraction: (8 − 2)² = 36, then 36 ÷ 9 = 4. Do not stop there: add the 5 to get 5 + 4 = 9. Stopping at 4 misses the final addition.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Build the fraction first (bracket, then power, then divide), then add the 5.

guided_steps.done: The fraction was finished before adding the 5.

gold.hint: Work the root and the bracket (its power first), then multiply, then add.

misconceptions.message: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3 = 6. With 8 the bracket is 5, so 9 + 4 × 5 = 29. Using 6 gives a bracket of 3 and 9 + 12 = 21.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Work the root, the bracket (its power first), then the multiply, then the add.

guided_steps.done: Root, power, bracket, ×, then +.

gold.hint: Finish the fraction (bracket, power, divide), work the other power, then subtract.

misconceptions.message: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3 = 6. The fraction is 8² ÷ 4 = 16, so 16 − 8 = 8. Using 6 for 2³ gives 16 − 6 = 10.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Finish the fraction (bracket, power, divide), work the other power, then subtract.

guided_steps.done: Fraction finished and 2³ found before subtracting.

gold.hint: Do both powers first, then the multiply and the fraction, then add.

misconceptions.message: 3² means 3 × 3 = 9, not (2 × 3)² = 36. So 2 × 9 = 18, and 40 ÷ 2³ = 5, giving 18 + 5 = 23. Squaring 2 × 3 gives 36 + 5 = 41.
misconceptions.note: expect derived by committing the error

guided_steps.say: Do both powers first, then the × and the fraction, then add.

guided_steps.hint: Multiply 2 by 9. The power was only on the 3.

guided_steps.done: Both powers first, then × and ÷, then +.

bronze.title: Bronze: multiply and divide before add and subtract
steps: No brackets or powers here. Do all the × and ÷ first, then the + and −.
× and ÷ share one level: when both appear, work left to right. The same goes for + and −.
A common slip is going straight left to right. Always clear the × and ÷ before touching + or −.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: The ÷ was done before the +, so 13 is right.

silver.title: Silver: brackets and powers come first
steps: Now brackets and powers appear. Work out anything inside brackets first.
After brackets and powers, finish with × and ÷, then + and −, left to right.

gold.title: Gold: fraction bars and roots group before you divide
steps: A fraction bar acts like brackets: finish the whole top and the whole bottom, then divide.
Roots and powers count as indices: do them with the brackets, before × ÷ + −.
Powers catch people out: \(2^3\) means 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3.

opener.label: Before any rules
opener.display:
A taxi charges a £3 flag fee to start, then £2 for every mile.
Your trip is 4 miles.

steps.pre: Add the £3 flag fee. Total fare = £
steps.hint: £8 of miles plus the £3 to start.

steps.say: You worked out the miles (4 × 2 = 8) before adding the £3, without being told to. Written down, the fare is \(3 + 2 \times 4\). Read blindly left to right that would be 3 + 2 = 5, then × 4 = 20, which is wrong. Your instinct to multiply first IS the rule: multiplication before addition. BIDMAS lists the full running order: Brackets, Indices, Divide and Multiply, Add and Subtract.
No brackets or powers. Do the ÷ and × first, left to right, then the +.

steps.done: ÷ and × cleared left to right before the +. That was the whole point.

steps.say: Now a bracket and a power appear. Both come before the × and +.

steps.done: Bracket and power went first. Gone before any × or +.

steps.say: The fraction bar groups the top. Build the whole top, then divide, then finish.

steps.hint: Divide the top by the bottom, 4.

steps.done: Top of the fraction grouped before dividing. That is the gold move.
